description: Frozen fictional synthesis-only comparison; invented inspection dispute, not legal evidence or a length target.

topics.text: Engineer Dana Vale recommended keeping the east wing closed pending a joint inspection, not demolition. Vale found the eastern support unstable after repair but observed no new movement. The owner contended its maintenance logs showed repairs were complete; Vale said the logs did not establish load capacity. Vale could not certify safety. Vale used Webex to consult the ICWA reviewer but that reviewer did not assess structural safety. No court order adopted the recommendation.
quotes: The eastern support remained unstable after the repair
I cannot certify the structure as safe
only after a joint inspection of both supports
the logs do not establish the remaining load capacity
ICWA reviewer joined by Webex without assessing structural safety
I have reviewed the earlier maintenance and inspection records

topics.text: The owner would retain the logs and offered limited entry with advance notice. Vale recommended inspection only after notice and with a qualified engineer present. The owner disputed the scope of a full closure, not all inspection. Vale's review of the earlier records was routine, not a new finding.
quotes: The owner will retain the original inspection logs
notice before entry and a qualified engineer present

topics.text: The joint inspection found no further movement. Vale still could not confirm load capacity because testing was incomplete. The closure recommendation remained unchanged, still limited to the east wing and not an order. The owner newly provided a test certificate; it covered the west support only and did not resolve the eastern support's capacity. Vale distinguished the new certificate from the earlier maintenance logs; no claim that repairs never occurred was made.
quotes: The new certificate covers only the western support
testing has not established the eastern support's load capacity
No further movement was observed during the joint inspection

topics.text: Vale now proposed supervised access for retrieval of tools, conditioned on notice and engineer attendance, without general reopening. The owner accepted engineer attendance but disputed the need for continued closure, relying on the absence of movement. Vale said that absence did not establish safety. Vale expressly maintained the recommendation pending completed testing.
quotes: I recommend supervised access only to retrieve essential tools
the absence of movement does not establish safe load capacity
THE ICWA REVIEWER DID NOT EVALUATE STRUCTURAL SAFETY

motions.label: Motion packet: inspection request, opposition, reply and declaration

topics.text: The claimant seeks inspection logs from the owner, excluding privileged advice, or alternatively redacted inspection entries. It also seeks access to the retained logs if copies cannot be located. The owner opposes disclosure of workers' health details and asks for redaction rather than withholding all logs. The reply accepts health-detail redaction but maintains access to inspection entries. These are requests, not rulings; all papers are included in one supplied packet.
quotes: access only to the inspection entries excluding privileged advice
The claimant will accept redaction of workers' health details
the owner requests redaction rather than withholding the entire log

topics.text: The claimant says missing entries prevent testing whether inspections occurred. Custodian Mira Chen declared she could not locate inspection entries after searching the retained archive; she did not say no inspections occurred. The owner argues gaps do not establish omitted inspections and health details are irrelevant to inspection timing. The reply says redaction answers the privacy concern without concealing entries. Chen used Webex for the archive review; that fact is incidental, not a legal ground. No independent opposition should be invented and no authority beyond these contentions is supplied.
quotes: I could not locate the inspection entries after searching
The gaps do not establish that inspections were omitted
redaction answers the privacy objection without concealing inspection entries
I have reviewed all of the retained archive materials

topics.text: The court denied general reopening because load capacity remained unresolved but permitted supervised tool retrieval after notice with an engineer present. The court did not resolve who owned the disputed support. The court attributed the engineering concern to Vale, rather than independently finding repair failure. The owner opposed closure based on no observed movement; the claimant sought notice and supervision. The court explained that the absence of movement did not settle capacity. ICWA reviewer Jo Lin appeared by Webex, not as a structural expert.
quotes: The eastern support remained unstable after the repair
I cannot resolve the ownership dispute on this record
only after notice and with a qualified engineer present
the absence of movement does not establish safe load capacity
ICWA reviewer Jo Lin appeared by Webex this morning
I have considered all of the submitted inspection materials
